parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *Posh Pets Spain (PPS)* is a pet hotel in the village of Alhaurin el Grande, Spain. It is run by Rachel Goutorbe, an animal enthusiast, and her team of four pet specialists. *PPS* offers overnight accommodation with room for seven dogs or cats, a pet grooming service and a shop selling pet products, such as dog coats and dog leads. Pet grooming involves washing, cutting and combing a pet’s coat.

Which **one **of the following is protected by legislation?

Select **one **answer.
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is B - Age**

Age is a protected characteristic under equality legislation, meaning employers cannot discriminate against employees or job applicants on the basis of their age.

**A** is incorrect as skills are not protected by legislation

**C** is incorrect as experience is not protected by legislation

**D** is incorrect as ability is not protected by legislation

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *TUI* is a holiday business that has over 100 years of experience. It offers customers a variety of holidays including staying in hotels, and river and ocean-going cruises. There are many extras that it offers to holiday makers including: car hire, extensions to the holiday and arranging day trips at all its holiday destinations.
> 
> The business is well known and flies its customers to over 180 destinations around the world, including Greece, Turkey and Spain. It has 1,600 travel agencies and 27 million customers. Holidays can be booked by visiting a travel agency or online.
> 
> *TUI* has holidays to meet the needs of all its customers: families, children, couples and those with disabilities.

State **one **reason why *TUI* pays its employees above the minimum wage.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for a valid reason why *TUI* pays its employees above the minimum wage in the context of the business
> 
> - To motivate TUI's employees to deliver good customer service to holidaymakers **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Employees are more likely to remain with *TUI* and their knowledge of cruises and holidays will not be lost **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - To attract skilled travel workers to *TUI* **[1 mark]**
> 
> Do not accept a reason that is not in the context of *TUI*.
> 
> Accept any appropriate response.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your answer is linked to the context of *TUI* — a generic reason such as "to motivate employees" without any reference to the travel or holiday industry will not be awarded the mark. Think about what makes *TUI*'s business specific (e.g. cruises, holidays, travel agencies) and connect your reason to that context.

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *TUI* has employees throughout the world. Some are employed to greet customers arriving at their holiday destination by air, rail or road. Others sell trips and excursions to customers once they reach their holiday destination. *TUI* prides itself on looking after all its employees and making sure that their needs are met.

State **one **reason why *TUI* would employ casual employees.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for a valid reason why *TUI* employs casual staff in the context of the business
> 
> - To meet increased demand for staff during peak holiday seasons **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - If an employee is off sick at a holiday resort someone is needed to cover the greeting of customers arriving at holiday hotels **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - During busy times when there are many people taking holidays extra employees may be needed to sell tours and excursions **[1 mark]**
> 
> Do not accept a reason that is not in the context of *TUI*
> 
> Accept any appropriate response

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your answer is linked to the context of *TUI* as a holiday company. A generic reason for employing casual staff that could apply to any business may not be awarded the mark. Think about what makes *TUI*'s staffing needs unique — for example, seasonal demand or covering absences at holiday destinations.

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *Saha *is a small business in Türkiye (formerly known as Turkey) that opened in 2020 with 15 employees. It designs and manufactures robots which are used in hospitals, hotels and restaurants. In hospitals its robots are used to move medical supplies between departments. In hotels and restaurants, the robots are used to welcome customers as they arrive and deliver food and drinks to hotel rooms and restaurant tables. *Saha *provides a seven day a week customer service for all businesses buying its robots.
> 
> Many new businesses are entering the global robot market and are competing for market share. Competitors in Türkiye include *NIO*, *Zoox *and *Vention*.
> 
> *Saha *has ambitious growth plans and has started to design robots that will be used in the home to help people with cleaning, shopping, security and entertainment. It aims to become a multinational business within five years to manufacture robots in all continents of the world.

Which **one **of the following is provided by a person applying for a job?

Select **one** answer.
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is B**

A curriculum vitae (CV) is a document prepared and provided by a person applying for a job, outlining their qualifications, experience and skills.

**A** is incorrect as a job description is provided to a job applicant by a business

**C** is incorrect as a person specification is provided to a job applicant by a business

**D** is incorrect as disciplinary and grievance procedures will be supplied to the successful candidate

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *Saha *is a small business in Türkiye (formerly known as Turkey) that opened in 2020 with 15 employees. It designs and manufactures robots which are used in hospitals, hotels and restaurants. In hospitals its robots are used to move medical supplies between departments. In hotels and restaurants, the robots are used to welcome customers as they arrive and deliver food and drinks to hotel rooms and restaurant tables. *Saha *provides a seven day a week customer service for all businesses buying its robots.
> 
> Many new businesses are entering the global robot market and are competing for market share. Competitors in Türkiye include NIO, Zoox and Vention.
> 
> *Saha *has ambitious growth plans and has started to design robots that will be used in the home to help people with cleaning, shopping, security and entertainment. It aims to become a multinational business within five years to manufacture robots in all continents of the world.

Outline **one **reason why *Saha *may dismiss an employee.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any pair from (1 mark per point):
> 
> - An employee may be dismissed for gross misconduct **[1 mark]**
> - Such as stealing from *Saha* or behaving violently towards a colleague, which would make it impossible for the business to continue employing them **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - An employee may be dismissed for poor performance **[1 mark]**
> - For example if a *Saha* worker repeatedly makes errors when designing robots that cause them to malfunction, despite receiving warnings **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - An employee's role may become redundant **[1 mark]**
> - For example if *Saha* introduces automated machinery that removes the need for certain manufacturing jobs **[1 mark]**
> 
> Award 1 mark for identifying a valid reason for dismissal and 1 mark for development of the reason in context.
> 
> Accept any other appropriate response.
> 
> "Outline" requires a brief statement of the key point plus some development or context.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you do more than just state a reason for dismissal — you need to develop your point by linking it to *Saha* or providing a relevant example. For instance, simply writing "gross misconduct" would only earn one mark. To gain the second mark, explain what this might look like in the context of *Saha*, such as an employee stealing equipment or behaving violently. Always try to refer back to the business in the extract to show the examiner you can apply your knowledge.

**[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md: Define the term **job description**.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - A document that outlines/sets out the duties/tasks and responsibilities of a particular job role **[1 mark]**
> 
> Award 1 mark for a correct definition of job description.
> 
> Acceptable alternative: a written document that sets out the tasks, responsibilities and expectations of a specific job within a business.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you focus on what a job description contains — duties, tasks and responsibilities — rather than confusing it with a person specification, which describes the qualities and qualifications needed in a candidate. A common mistake is to mix up these two documents.

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> The first *Premier Inn *hotel was opened in 1987. *Premier Inn *now has over 820 hotels in the UK, United Arab Emirates (UAE) and India with over 83,000 rooms. It has recently expanded by opening the first* Premier Inn* in Germany and has plans to open more in other countries.

State **one **reason why *Premier Inn* uses seasonal employees.

> 
> OR

> - To avoid the cost of employing permanent staff during quieter periods when fewer guests are staying at *Premier Inn* **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - To increase staffing levels during busy periods such as school holidays without increasing *Premier Inn*'s long-term wage costs **[1 mark]**

>

A generic reason such as "to have more staff when busy" without any reference to the business context will not earn the mark. > **[mark-scheme]**
> - An application form allows *Premier Inn* to gather information about a candidate's skills and experience **[1 mark]**
> - So that it can compare applicants against the requirements of the job and decide who to invite for an interview **[1 mark]**

> OR

Make sure your second point clearly builds on and extends your first point rather than introducing a completely separate idea. parts.problem_md: Define the term **person specification**.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - A person specification is a document that outlines the skills, qualifications and personal qualities required from a candidate applying for a job **[1 mark]**
> 
> Award 1 mark for a correct definition of person specification.
> 
> Alternative acceptable answer:
> 
> - A person specification is a document that describes the ideal characteristics, experience and attributes that a business is looking for in a job applicant

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your definition refers to the qualities or attributes of the *person* rather than the duties of the job — that would describe a job description instead. A common mistake is confusing a person specification with a job description. Remember, a person specification focuses on the ideal candidate (e.g. their skills, qualifications and experience), while a job description focuses on the role itself.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *IKEA* is a well-known home furniture retailer with stores throughout the world. It was started in 1943 by Ingvar Kamprad when he was given some money by his father for doing well at school. He wanted to produce furniture at a price that people could afford to buy.
> 
> He realised that transporting furniture to customers was difficult as goods were often damaged. He developed flat packs to avoid damage. A flat pack contained all the materials needed to self-assemble a table, a chair or a bed.
> 
> All *IKEA *stores are run as franchises.

One of *IKEA’s *aims is to keep up to date with the changes taking place in product design and meeting customers’ needs. To do this it has to introduce new and different products on a regular basis.

State **one **reason why *IKEA *would employ temporary staff.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any 1 from:
> 
> - To meet increased demand during busy shopping periods such as Christmas **[1 mark]**
> - To cover for permanent IKEA employees who are absent due to illness or holiday **[1 mark]**
> - To provide additional staff when IKEA opens a new store in a different location **[1 mark]**
> 
> Accept any other appropriate response in the context of IKEA.
> 
> Marks are not awarded for a reason that is not in the context of IKEA.
> 
> "State" requires a brief, clear point without further explanation.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you relate your answer specifically to IKEA rather than giving a generic reason for employing temporary staff. For example, referring to busy shopping periods at IKEA stores or covering for absent permanent staff at IKEA demonstrates that you understand the context of the business. A vague answer such as "because they need more workers" without linking it to IKEA is unlikely to earn the mark.

parts.problem_md:

> Accept any other appropriate response.

Make sure your answer has two distinct parts: a clear point about why seasonal staff are useful during harvesting, and then a linked explanation of the benefit this brings to NOF. Many students lose the second mark by simply restating their first point in different words rather than extending it — try to explain the consequence or advantage for the business. Think about what would happen if NOF used permanent staff instead, as this can help you frame your development point.

**[2 marks]**

> **[case-study]**

*Premier Inn* has employees across the world. When a new position becomes available, *Premier Inn* must make sure that the recruitment method used is the correct one for the vacant position. It is considering the following two options:

**Option 2:** external recruitment, by using an employment agency

parts.solution_md:
Recruitment is the process of finding and attracting suitable candidates to fill a job vacancy **[K]**. Internal recruitment means Premier Inn would fill the position with an existing employee from one of its 820 hotels worldwide **[Ap]**. With hotels across the UK, UAE, India and Germany**[Ap]**, moving staff between locations could also be costly and disruptive, and it does not bring any fresh  ideas or new skills into the business **[An]**

External recruitment through an employment agency would give Premier Inn access to a much wider pool of candidates **[K]** with different skills and experience. This could be especially useful as Premier Inn expands into new countries like Germany**[Ap]**, where local candidates may better understand the culture and language of the market **[An]**

On the other hand, using an employment agency can be expensive **[K]**, as agencies charge fees for finding candidates. External recruits will also need more training to learn how Premier Inn operates, which takes time and could temporarily affect the quality of service provided to hotel guests **[Ap] [An]**

Premier Inn should choose Option 1, internal recruitment **[E]**. Since Premier Inn wants to retain its employees **[Ap]**, promoting from within rewards loyalty and motivates staff to stay with the company. External recruitment through an agency is costly and risky when maintaining consistent service standards across a growing global business is the priority **[E]**

> - Internal promotion signals to all Premier Inn staff that hard work is rewarded → increases motivation across the workforce → helping Premier Inn retain more employees and reduce recruitment costs long term
